name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Crowd Control SMG ACSM-3 'Shepherd'
description:
The ACSM-3 Shepherd is a dual-feed SMG that accepts two magazines simultaneously — one loaded with lethal 9mm caseless rounds and one with rubber-composite less-lethal projectiles. The BCI fire-control system allows the operator to switch between lethal and less-lethal ammunition through neural command, selecting the appropriate response to each individual in a crowd without changing weapons or magazines.

The weapon's BCI overlay integrates with Arcturus' crowd-analysis AI, which categorizes individuals in real-time as passive, agitated, or hostile. The system recommends lethal or less-lethal response for each categorized individual, and the operator confirms or overrides per-target. In practice, a Shepherd operator can fire rubber rounds at protesters while switching to lethal ammunition for armed individuals within the same trigger squeeze.

Arcturus designed the Shepherd for corporate police crowd-control operations, replacing the two-weapon system (lethal rifle plus less-lethal launcher) with a single platform. At Φ5,500, the weapon is institutional procurement only. The dual-feed mechanism is mechanically complex and requires regular maintenance, but the tactical flexibility it provides has made the ACSM-3 standard issue for Arcturus crowd-management units.
specifications:
caliber: 9mm caseless (lethal) / 9mm rubber-composite (less-lethal)
effective_range: 50m (lethal), 30m (less-lethal)
rate_of_fire: 600 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 20+20 rounds (dual magazine)
weight: 2.7 kg
tactical_use: The Shepherd allows continuous crowd-control operations with escalating force options available per trigger pull. Operators can suppress non-lethal threats with rubber rounds while immediately engaging armed threats with lethal ammunition, maintaining a single point of aim and eliminating the delay of weapon transitions. The crowd-analysis AI provides real-time threat categorization, but operators retain final authority on ammunition selection for each target.
cultural_context: The Shepherd is the most visible weapon of corporate crowd control. Its dual-feed system has been criticized as enabling casual escalation — the ease of switching between lethal and less-lethal ammunition lowers the psychological barrier to lethal force. Protesters have learned to identify Shepherd operators by the distinctive dual-magazine profile, and the weapon has become a symbol of the corporate police state's capacity for selective violence within crowds.
story_hooks: A Shepherd operator's BCI was hacked to display all crowd members as 'hostile' — the operator fired lethal rounds into a peaceful protest before realizing the overlay was compromised.
The crowd-analysis AI has been trained on biased data that categorizes certain demographics as 'agitated' regardless of their actual behavior, leading to discriminatory less-lethal targeting.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular SMG with an aggressive forward-swept profile. Twin magazine wells dominate the lower receiver, creating a distinctly wider footprint than conventional firearms. The weapon reads as utilitarian and purposeful—all function, minimal ornamentation. The dual-feed system gives it a boxer's stance: squared shoulders, centered weight distribution.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 38cm | Barrel length: 12.7cm | Width at magazine well: 6.2cm | Height (with charging handle): 11cm
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and front-heavy (2.7kg). The dual magazines and BCI module shift mass toward the grip, creating natural pointing geometry. Feels authoritative in hand without excess bulk—designed for sustained operation during long crowd-control deployments.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer frame (DuPont Zytel HD) with integrated steel barrel shroud and dual-feed cycling mechanism. Upper receiver is aluminum 7075-T6 with hard-anodized treatment for durability under constant handling.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed steel accents around the dual magazine wells and feed mechanism. The BCI integration port (rear receiver junction) features a subtle iridescent coating that catches light—marking it as a 'smart' weapon system.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant charcoal-black polymer with steel-gray feed system accents. Faint corporate blue piping along the rail system indicates Arcturus branding. Rubber overmold grips in tactical gray.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured rubber overmold—sharp diamond pattern for secure purchase in gloved or augmented hands. Magazine well edges finished in knurled steel for positive magazine changes during high-stress operations.
distinctive_features: Dual magazine wells with independent feed indicators on each (small red/green witness dots)
BCI neural-interface port: smooth, recessed chrome node at rear of receiver—barely visible unless actively interfacing
Integrated crowd-analysis display: small holographic pop-up on left rail (dimmed when inactive, glowing soft blue during operation)
Charging handle: dual-sided, oversized for gloved operation, with heat-venting ribbed design
Magazine identification grooves: lethal mags marked with subtle raised 'L' symbol; less-lethal marked with 'R' symbol
Muzzle brake with integral flash suppressor featuring visible baffles designed to reduce less-lethal round tumble
Heat vents along the barrel shroud—a necessary feature for sustained crowd-control fire rates
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS in embossed sans-serif along the left receiver rail. Model designation ACSM-3 stamped below the ejection port. Serial number on a small stainless steel plate inset into the right side of the frame. Small Arcturus circular logo (concentric rings with sword motif) etched into the magazine well area.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained with visible wear patterns. Scuff marks on the polymer grip from gloved handling. The BCI port shows light contact marks from neural-interface connections. Muzzle area exhibits faint carbon buildup from mixed-ammunition cycles. Overall: battle-ready but institutional—equipment of a working corporate police unit, not a black-market operator.
